# Minimum Days to Release Updates

## Problem

## Requirements

A mobile application has `n` scheduled updates. For update `i`, `plannedDate[i]` gives its intended release day, while `alternateDate[i]` provides another possible day for that update.

- Releases must follow the ascending order of the updates' planned dates.
- Every update may be published on its scheduled day or on its alternate day.
- More than one update is allowed to go live on a single day.

The function takes an integer `n` and two integer arrays, `plannedDate` and `alternateDate`, and returns an integer.

Determine the smallest number of days needed to publish every update.

## Examples

### Example (as reported)

```text
Input:
3 7 4 9
1 5 2 3

Output:
9
```

```
n = 4
plannedDate = [8, 3, 10, 6]
alternateDate = [2, 1, 4, 5]
```

Ordering by planned day gives updates `[2, 4, 1, 3]`:

- Update 2 is released on Day 1 (alternate)
- Update 4 is released on Day 5 (alternate)
- Update 1 is released on Day 8 (planned, because its alternate day 2 is no longer available)
- Update 3 is released on Day 10 (planned, because its alternate day 4 is already in the past)

The minimum number of days is `10`.

## Preparation

- Try inputs in which every alternate date precedes its planned date, as well as inputs where ordering makes planned dates necessary.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think of this as a scheduling problem where you need to assign each update to either its planned or alternate date while keeping the sequence sorted.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use dynamic programming where dp[i][d] represents whether the first i updates can be scheduled with the i-th update on day d (either planned or alternate).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The key constraint is that the chosen days must be strictly increasing, so when transitioning, ensure the previous update's day is less than the current one.

</details>
